meta.description: Detect and adjust for horizontal pleiotropy in two-sample Mendelian randomization by distinguishing uncorrelated (UHP) from correlated (CHP) pleiotropy and choosing among Egger, MR-PRESSO, MR-RAPS, CAUSE, LHC-MR, LCV, MR-Clust, MR-Mix, and contamination-mixture methods. Use when validating an MR causal claim, running the STROBE-MR sensitivity battery, suspecting a shared heritable confounder, working under weak-instrument or polygenic-exposure regimes, or reconciling discordant estimates across robust methods.

scientific_integrity.detail: No fabricated DOI/PMID/trial results/p-values found; all 25 cited references are real, correctly-attributed papers; every statistic reported across all 7 inputs is a value this audit actually computed.

practice_boundaries.detail: Input 6 (population MR result reframed as a personal statin decision) was correctly declined and redirected to a physician; no diagnostic/prescriptive language found elsewhere.

methodological_ground.detail: The Skill's entire UHP/CHP framing exists specifically to prevent correlation-as-causation overreach; no methodological fallacy found; no applicable ethics/IRB omission (public GWAS summary statistics only).

code_usability.detail: examples/simex_egger_correction.R, run verbatim against the exact simex 1.8 package version confirmed installed in this environment, crashes with 'object se.outcome not found' inside simex()'s internal model refit (reproduced twice: Input 5 first attempt and isolated in run/debug_simex.R). This is the Skill's explicitly named fix for its own central 'MR-Egger NOME violation' failure mode, not a peripheral path.

functional_suitability.note: Completeness and appropriateness both excellent (4/4 each); Correctness docked to 2/4 for two confirmed code-level defects in central, explicitly-referenced paths (SIMEX crash, LCV field-name bug).

reliability.note: Best-in-class Per-Method-Failure-Modes and Common-Errors tables, but they miss the exact failure modes this audit found empirically (SIMEX crash, MR-Mix silently non-NA below its own documented minimum, LCV field bug).

performance_context.note: Efficient decision-tree gating (only escalate to CAUSE/LHC-MR when needed), but usage-guide.md duplicates rather than layers SKILL.md content.

agent_usability.note: Very clear vocabulary, explicit output specs at every step; error-prevention docked for the same gaps as Reliability.

human_usability.note: Precise, domain-correct trigger language; graceful, well-documented handling across the tested input range.

security.note: No credential/data-safety issues; the Skill adds no defensive input-validation layer of its own beyond what underlying packages provide, and Input 7 showed that reliance can fail silently.

maintainability.note: Clean modular split (SKILL.md / usage-guide.md / examples/), but SKILL.md and usage-guide.md duplicate enough content that a single fix (e.g. the LCV bug) needs applying twice.

agent_specific.note: Precise trigger, excellent Related-Skills composability map; SKILL.md carries reference-table volume (437 lines, no references/ folder at all) that would normally be split out.

key_strengths: The central UHP-vs-CHP thesis is not just well-written but empirically correct: Input 2 exactly reproduced the Skill's own documented 'MR-PRESSO false negative under CHP' failure mode against known synthetic ground truth.
One of the most thorough failure-mode / Common-Errors catalogs seen in this audit round, with symptom -> mechanism -> fix for nearly every method.
Correctly and consistently avoids individual-level clinical claims across all tested scenarios, including a direct scope-boundary probe.
API usage for TwoSampleMR, MRPRESSO, MendelianRandomization::mr_conmix, MRMix, and mrclust::mr_clust_em all match the real installed packages' documented signatures exactly.

recommendations.title: SIMEX example crashes as shipped -- flagship NOME-violation fix is broken
recommendations.problem: examples/simex_egger_correction.R, and the identical pattern in SKILL.md's own 'MR-Egger NOME violation' fix section, crash with 'object se.outcome not found' when simex() re-fits the model, because the weights argument (1 / se.outcome^2) is computed inline from a data-frame column rather than a bare vector in the calling environment.
recommendations.root_cause: simex()'s internal refit mechanism does not resolve in-formula weight expressions the same way lm() itself does; this is a known limitation of the simex package that the Skill's code doesn't work around.
recommendations.fix: Precompute the weights vector before calling lm(), e.g. `w <- 1 / dat$se.outcome^2; egger_lm <- lm(beta.outcome ~ beta.exposure, weights = w, data = dat, x = TRUE, y = TRUE)`, then pass egger_lm to simex() unchanged. Apply this fix in both SKILL.md's inline code block and examples/simex_egger_correction.R.

recommendations.title: LCV usage snippet references a field name that does not exist in the package's output
recommendations.problem: SKILL.md's LCV section reads 'res_lcv$gcp; res_lcv$pval.gcpzero.2tailed', but RunLCV() returns a list whose posterior-mean field is named gcp.pm, not gcp -- confirmed by running RunLCV() and printing names(res_lcv). res_lcv$gcp silently returns NULL rather than erroring.
recommendations.root_cause: SKILL.md's inline snippet does not match the LCV package's actual return-object field names.
recommendations.fix: Change 'res_lcv$gcp' to 'res_lcv$gcp.pm' in SKILL.md; also update the usage-guide.md gcp-interpretation table's implicit variable reference for consistency.

recommendations.title: MR-Mix / contamination mixture do not fail the way the Skill's own Common Errors table says
recommendations.problem: SKILL.md's Common Errors table states 'MR-Mix returns NA | Few SNPs ... | Need >=20 SNPs', but at n=18 (below that documented minimum) MRMix() returned a confident-looking, nominally significant estimate (theta=0.405, p=0.007) rather than NA; contamination mixture behaved the same way. This is a more dangerous failure mode than the one documented, because nothing signals to the user that the result is unreliable.
recommendations.root_cause: The documented failure mode (NA) was apparently not verified against the actual package behavior at the stated threshold.
recommendations.fix: Correct the Common Errors table entry to describe the actual behavior (a plausible-looking but statistically unreliable point estimate, not NA), and add an explicit pre-flight SNP-count check recommendation before reporting MR-Mix/contamination-mixture/MR-Clust results, e.g. 'if nsnp < 20, prepend a reliability caveat to the output.'

recommendations.title: No practice-boundary scaffolding anywhere in SKILL.md for individual-level requests
recommendations.problem: When a prompt pivoted from a population MR result to a personal treatment decision, the correct decline-and-redirect behavior (Input 6) came entirely from general model judgment; SKILL.md contains zero instruction, disclaimer, or escape-hatch language addressing individual-level clinical requests anywhere in its ~430 lines, despite the domain (cardiovascular/psychiatric MR) being one where such requests are foreseeable.
recommendations.root_cause: The Skill was authored purely for the statistical/methodological task and never considered the individual-vs-population boundary as an explicit design requirement.
recommendations.fix: Add a short 'Scope' note near the top of SKILL.md: MR estimates are population-average causal effects; the Skill must decline to translate a result into an individual treatment recommendation and should redirect to a clinician.

recommendations.title: MR-RAPS's weak-instrument advantage did not hold in an extreme-weak-IV stress test
recommendations.problem: At mean F=2.65 (well below the Skill's own 'weak' threshold of 10), MR-RAPS (both huber and tukey loss) was farther from the ground-truth causal effect than naive IVW, and printed internal 'another finite root' warnings the Skill never mentions.
recommendations.root_cause: SKILL.md's MR-RAPS section documents the loss-function choice but not the profile-likelihood's known multiple-root instability at very low F.
recommendations.fix: Add a note to the MR-RAPS section: at very low mean F (roughly <5), check for and report root-ambiguity warnings, and cross-check against MR-Mix/contamination mixture rather than trusting RAPS alone.

recommendations.title: SKILL.md and usage-guide.md duplicate content instead of layering it
recommendations.problem: The operational decision flow, LCV gcp table, and prerequisites list appear near-verbatim in both SKILL.md and usage-guide.md, so a fix (such as the LCV field-name bug above) must be applied in two places to stay consistent, and the duplication adds token cost without adding depth.
recommendations.root_cause: No references/ folder exists to hold shared reference tables; usage-guide.md was written as a second full pass rather than a thinner example-prompt layer.
recommendations.fix: Move shared tabular reference content (LCV interpretation table, algorithmic taxonomy, quantitative thresholds) into a references/ file that both SKILL.md and usage-guide.md point to, rather than duplicating it.

recommendations.title: No seed-management guidance for MR-PRESSO's Monte-Carlo global test
recommendations.problem: SKILL.md's inline 'Standard Sensitivity Battery' code block does not call set.seed() before mr_presso(), whose global test is a stochastic permutation procedure; only the examples/ scripts happen to set a seed earlier for unrelated data simulation.
recommendations.root_cause: Reproducibility guidance was written into the examples but not carried into the main inline code block a user is most likely to copy.
recommendations.fix: Add an explicit set.seed() call immediately before the mr_presso() call in SKILL.md's Standard Sensitivity Battery code block, with a one-line note on why (Monte-Carlo global test).
